evidence.quote: coral reef and ocean monitoring. The satellite must provide images for a fluid lensing tool
only one satellite is required. This also just allows for simplicity
likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.reasoning: Primary mission (coral reef monitoring benefiting Australia), single spacecraft rationale (bleaching over days/weeks), users/operators clearly stated with context, supported by references. Meets all required info to high standard.

evidence.quote: proposed satellite will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle – launched from the Guiana Space Centre
altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924° for the satellite to remain sun-synchronous

criteria.reasoning: Demonstrates adequate understanding: launch vehicle/site with rationale, SSO orbit type, 600km altitude, inclination calculation and table of elements, maneuver note, ground station with STK access report, EOL drag sail. Some errors: RAAN described as launch facility location, Arg of lat misuse, swath not quantified, comm frequency band missing, Vega E not yet flown but used as definitive choice. Evidence present (Image 1-5, plots, tables).

evidence.quote: fully described satellite configuration has been constructed. The initial problem of not catching coral bleaching events

criteria.reasoning: Conclusion summarizes mission segments and reiterates launch, orbit, ground station and benefit but lacks quantitative conclusions drawn from STK results (e.g., coverage performance, contact duration stats) and risk/mitigation. Generic but appropriate.

Has logical structure, headings, figures labelled partially, readable but formatting inconsistent (tables broken, STK screenshots lacking titles), uses Wikipedia despite prohibition, references not properly formatted, executive summary present but not concise. Meets adequate level.

technical_issues.issue: RAAN value 27.33° linked to launch facility latitude, incorrect definition; Argument of Latitude used to replace AOP/ν but not valid classic element set; e=0 claim circular but J2 perturbed SSO typically slightly eccentric; no communication frequency band defined despite requirement.

Selects Vega E (first flight 2024 planned, not yet proven in 2020 assignment) without performance verification or mass budget; equatorial launch benefit argument applied to SSO retrograde which reduces benefit; references Wikipedia timeline as primary source despite ban.
Access report shows mean ~580s contact but fails to compute daily communication opportunities/revisit to GBR; no link budget, frequency, or data rate.

overall: Solid mission concept with good rationale for Australia, single-sat SSO justified, STK evidence included. Minor technical inaccuracies and missing comms details keep it at adequate rather than accomplished overall.
